Task:
Bug report: when reading a CSV line, a quoted field that contains a comma, like "Smith, John", is split into two columns. Quoted fields must stay one field (without the quotes), and a doubled quote "" inside a quoted field is one quote character. split_line('1,"Smith, John",3') == ["1", "Smith, John", "3"] split_line('"say ""hi""",x') == ['say "hi"', "x"] plain lines still split all checks pass

Candidate files:
- io_utils/csv_writer.py: io_utils/csv_writer.py Write rows as CSV: fields with a comma or a quote are quoted, quotes doubled. def quote_field(field: str) -> str def write_line(fields: list[str]) -> str
- io_utils/csv_reader.py: io_utils/csv_reader.py Read CSV text into rows of fields. def split_line(line: str) -> list[str] def read_rows(text: str) -> list[list[str]]
- io_utils/tsv_reader.py: io_utils/tsv_reader.py Read TSV lines (fields split on tabs). def split_tsv_line(line: str) -> list[str]
- parsers/quotes.py: parsers/quotes.py Smart quotes -> plain quotes in text fields. def plain_quotes(text: str) -> str
- legacy/csv_split_old.py: legacy/csv_split_old.py DEPRECATED: the first CSV splitter (no quotes support). Use io_utils.csv_reader. def old_split(line: str) -> list[str]
- report.py: report.py Summary of a CSV file: number of rows and columns. def shape(text: str) -> tuple[int, int] io_utils.csv_reader
